primitives.name: Expected Goals
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study develops a documented framework for estimating expected goals (xG) and attributing recorded offensive value in the National Lacrosse League, using 1,006 manually annotated Rochester Knighthawks shot attempts, including 151 goals, from thirteen consecutive games played between January 3 and April 4 of the 2025–2026 season.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'binary indicator for goal scored (0 or 1)', 'S': 'shot event with spatial and temporal features', '\\mathbf{x}_s': 'feature vector of shot context', '\\sigma': 'logistic sigmoid function'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot outcomes are conditionally independent given context; logistic regression captures non-linear relationships in shot features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When shot context lacks discriminative power beyond base rate, model performance degrades.

layer2.mapping: xG serves as kernel for probabilistic attribution of offensive value in GSI's Bayesian belief update.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score and log loss from Leave-One-Game-Out CV.

primitives.name: Expected Assists
primitives.verbatim_quote: The probabilities support attribution through xG for shooters and shot-based expected assists for recorded final passers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'expected assist value', 'P': 'passing action', 'S': 'set of shots', '\\mathbb{P}(G | s)': 'probability of goal given shot', '\\mathbb{P}(P \\to s)': 'probability of pass leading to shot'}
primitives.assumptions: Passes are temporally and spatially linked to shots; assist value is additive across passes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pass-to-shot mapping is ambiguous or missing, xA estimation fails.

layer2.mapping: xA mirrors xG in structure but applies to passers instead of shooters, enabling isomorphic attribution in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation accuracy of pass-based xG models.

primitives.name: Expected Pick Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: A counterfactual Expected Pick Value (xPV) for qualifying pickers compares the recorded state with the same row after the pick fields are set to their no-pick values.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{xPV}': 'expected pick value in goals', 'P_{\\text{with pick}}': 'pass with pick action', 'P_{\\text{no pick}}': 'pass without pick action'}
primitives.assumptions: Counterfactuals are valid under stable game dynamics; pick actions are causally separable from other actions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pick actions are confounded with other game events, xPV becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: xPV provides a kernel for evaluating strategic impact of pick actions in GSE’s state-space planning.
layer2.telemetry: Permutation test p-values for xPV significance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The framework integrates shot-level data into a probabilistic model using logistic regression, random forests, and extremely randomized trees. Shot features include spatial coordinates, timing, and situational context. The xG model estimates goal probability per shot, enabling attribution of offensive value to players. The xA extends this by assigning assist-like values to passers based on shot likelihood. The xPV introduces a counterfactual mechanism to evaluate the impact of pick actions. All primitives rely on Leave-One-Game-Out cross-validation for robustness, yet the small sample size limits generalizability. The framework's dual nature—estimating both outcome and contribution—enables a dualistic view of offensive performance. Failure modes arise when context is insufficient or when actions are not independently identifiable. The use of ensemble models mitigates overfitting but introduces complexity in interpretation. The framework thus represents a hybrid of descriptive and predictive analytics, suitable for tactical analysis but not causal inference.
